process_area.title: Supply Chain Network Strategy, Modeling & Design

value_stream.name: Supply Chain Network Design, Multi-Echelon Inventory Optimization & Flow Engineering

fields.Owner: VP Supply Chain / Network Strategy Lead
fields.Participants: COO, Strategy (VS-33), Real Estate (VS-97/VS-20), Finance (VS-17.4), Merchandising (VS-01)
fields.Trigger: Strategy refresh; growth; major cost/service pressure

workflows.name: Supply Chain Network Strategy & Design Principles

Controls: - CTL-638 (ensure controlled execution — Supply Chain Network Strategy, Modeling & Design (PA-136.1).)
- CTL-638: network strategy approved by COO/Board; trade-off guardrails documented
Cross-references: - links to VS-33 (strategy), VS-37 (growth), VS-97/VS-20 (real estate), VS-110 (freight cost)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Drift risk**: Network evolves ad-hoc without strategy; mitigated by documented principles and annual review
- **Sub-optimization risk**: Optimizing one dimension (e.g., cost) harms another (service); mitigated by explicit trade-off guardrails
System Touchpoints: - Strategy (VS-33); network modeling (W4122); finance/cost-to-serve (VS-17.4/VS-110); real estate (VS-97/VS-20)

steps.activity: Network Strategy define the network strategy and design principles (cost-to-serve, service-level, resilience, scalability to 300+ stores, sustainability), aligned to corporate strategy (VS-33) and the growth plan (10–15 stores/yr links to VS-37)
Network Strategy document the current-state network (DCs, cross-dock, DSD, store-receiving, lane map), service levels, and cost-to-serve baseline
Network Strategy set design targets and trade-off guardrails (cost vs service vs working-capital vs capex), and present to the executive team

fields.Owner: Network Strategy Lead / Supply Chain Analytics (VS-28)
fields.Participants: Analytics (VS-28), Supply Planning (VS-02), Finance (VS-17.4), Real Estate (VS-97)
fields.Trigger: Network decision; growth; disruption; what-if question

workflows.name: Network Modeling, Scenario Simulation & What-If Analysis

Automation Opportunity: - Model auto-refresh from ERP/BI; scenario templating; sensitivity automation
Controls: - CTL-638 (ensure controlled execution — Supply Chain Network Strategy, Modeling & Design (PA-136.1).)
- CTL-638: model assumptions documented and validated; results reviewed by Finance/SC leadership
Cross-references: - links to VS-127 (S&OP), VS-02 (supply), VS-28 (analytics), VS-29 (MDM)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Garbage-in risk**: Model outputs driven by bad demand/cost data; mitigated by data-quality governance (VS-28.2)
- **Black-box risk**: Model not trusted/understood; mitigated by transparency and validation against actuals
System Touchpoints: - Network optimization/simulation tool; BI/analytics (VS-28); demand planning (VS-127/VS-02); master data (VS-29); GIS

steps.activity: Network Strategy/Analytics build and maintain the network model (demand by location, DC/store nodes, lanes, lead times, cost, capacity, inventory) fed by demand planning (VS-127/VS-02) and master data (VS-29)
Network Strategy run scenarios (new DC, DC closure, store growth, port change, modal shift, service-level change), and quantify cost/service/working-capital impact
Network Strategy present scenario results, recommend, and feed decisions into network design (W4123–W4127) and business cases (W4128)

fields.Participants: DC Ops (VS-04), Real Estate (VS-97/VS-20), Finance/Capex (VS-40), Supply Planning (VS-02)
fields.Trigger: Growth; capacity strain; DC add/close decision
fields.Volume: Enterprise DC network (4 DCs; Clark DC4 oversized for growth)

Controls: - CTL-638 (ensure controlled execution — Supply Chain Network Strategy, Modeling & Design (PA-136.1).)
- CTL-638: DC add/close via capex governance (VS-40) and Board approval (VS-36)
Cross-references: - links to VS-04 (DC), VS-97/VS-20 (real estate), VS-40 (capex), VS-36 (governance)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Stranded-asset risk**: DC sized wrong (too big/small); mitigated by modeling and phased expansion
- **Island-coverage risk**: Archipelago gaps in coverage; mitigated by location optimization for island logistics
System Touchpoints: - Network model (W4122); DC ops (VS-04); real estate (VS-97/VS-20); capex (VS-40); GIS

steps.activity: Network Strategy/Real Estate assess DC footprint vs the growth plan (current 4 DCs; Clark oversized for North/Central Luzon expansion), capacity utilization, and the optimal number/location/size of DCs via modeling (W4122)
steps.r: Network Strategy Lead / Real Estate / DC Ops

steps.activity: Network Strategy/Real Estate evaluate add/close/expand/relocate options (cost-to-serve, service, capex links to VS-40, sustainability, risk), and recommend
steps.r: Network Strategy Lead / Finance / Real Estate

steps.activity: Network Strategy execute approved changes (DC opening/closure/expand links to VS-04/VS-20/VS-97), and track benefit (W4128/W4140)

fields.Trigger: New stores; DC change; service review

Controls: - CTL-638 (ensure controlled execution — Supply Chain Network Strategy, Modeling & Design (PA-136.1).)
- CTL-638: coverage decisions documented; service-level targets per territory
Cross-references: - links to VS-02 (supply), VS-06 (logistics), VS-37/VS-59 (open/close), VS-29 (location master)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Imbalance risk**: Some DCs overloaded, others under-utilized; mitigated by load-balanced assignment
- **Single-sourcing risk**: Store dependent on one DC (fragile); mitigated by backup sourcing (W4127)
System Touchpoints: - Network model (W4122); supply planning (VS-02); logistics routing (VS-06); location master (VS-29)

steps.activity: Network Strategy assign/optimise store-to-DC coverage (which DC serves which store), balancing distance/lead time/capacity/load via modeling (W4122)
Network Strategy define service areas (replenishment frequency 2–3x/week, delivery lead time 1–3 days links to VS-02), and handle multi-DC sourcing for constrained supply
Network Strategy update coverage on store openings (VS-37)/closures (VS-59), rebalance on DC change, and monitor service-level adherence (W4139)

fields.Trigger: Sourcing change; import growth; port disruption

workflows.name: Inbound Flow, Sourcing Lane & Port-of-Entry Design

Controls: - CTL-638 (ensure controlled execution — Supply Chain Network Strategy, Modeling & Design (PA-136.1).)
- CTL-638: lane decisions with landed-cost and customs review (VS-87/VS-110)
Cross-references: - links to VS-122 (sourcing), VS-87 (customs), VS-110 (freight), VS-02.2 (import), VS-02.3 (disruption)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Port-concentration risk**: Over-reliance on one port (congestion/typhoon); mitigated by multi-port design (W4127)
- **Duty/landed-cost risk**: Lane choice ignores duty/landed cost; mitigated by total-landed-cost modeling (VS-110/VS-13)
System Touchpoints: - Network model (W4122); import/customs (VS-02.2/VS-87); freight (VS-110); sourcing (VS-122); disruption (VS-02.3)

steps.activity: Network Strategy/Sourcing design inbound flow: source markets (links to VS-122), port-of-entry selection (Manila/Cebu/Cagayan/Davao), lane-to-DC assignment, and modal mix (ocean/inter-island/land)
Network Strategy/Freight optimize inbound lanes for cost/lead time/reliability/duty (links to VS-110/VS-87), and design consolidation (FCL/LCL, multi-vendor)
Network Strategy monitor lane performance (links to VS-110/W727 carrier monitoring), adjust on disruption (VS-02.3 W729), and incorporate into MEIO (W4130)

fields.Volume: ~5,000 store-replenishment orders/month; ~42,900 ecommerce orders/month; 200 stores × 2–3 deliveries/week

workflows.name: Outbound Distribution Flow & Lane / Routing Architecture

Automation Opportunity: - Route optimization engine; dynamic re-routing on disruption
Controls: - CTL-638 (ensure controlled execution — Supply Chain Network Strategy, Modeling & Design (PA-136.1).)
- CTL-638: routing changes reviewed; carrier SLA adherence (VS-110)
Cross-references: - links to VS-06 (logistics/routing), VS-110 (freight), VS-56 (last-mile), VS-04 (DC)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Under-utilization risk**: Partial loads (poor cube/weight utilization); mitigated by consolidation and routing optimization
- **Island-routing risk**: Inter-island complexity; mitigated by modal-aware routing
System Touchpoints: - Network model (W4122); logistics/routing (VS-06); freight (VS-110); last-mile (VS-56); WMS (VS-04)

steps.activity: Network Strategy/Logistics design the outbound flow architecture: DC-to-store lanes, multi-stop routing, modal mix (owned 20% / 3PL 80% trucks), and last-mile for ecommerce
Network Strategy/Logistics optimize routes for cost/service (links to VS-06 W786 route optimization, VS-110 freight), and design consolidation (replenishment grouping 2–3 orders/truck)
Network Strategy monitor outbound performance (OTIF, cost-per-stop, fill-rate W4139), adjust routing, and feed into network model (W4122)

fields.Trigger: Risk review; disruption event; resilience program

Controls: - CTL-80 (ensure inventory parameter & network optimization governance.)
- CTL-638: resilience design reviewed by Risk/BCP; single-source SKUs monitored
Cross-references: - links to VS-21.2 (ERM), VS-26 (BCP), VS-02.3 (supplier/disruption risk), W4143 (simulation)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Single-point-of-failure risk**: One disruption halts supply to stores; mitigated by redundancy design
- **Over-redundancy risk**: Excess redundancy inflates cost; mitigated by risk-based, cost-justified design
System Touchpoints: - Risk register (VS-21.2); BCP (VS-26); network model/simulation (W4122/W4143); supplier risk (VS-02.3)

steps.activity: Network Strategy/Risk assess network vulnerabilities (single-source SKUs, single-DC-served stores, single-port lanes, typhoon/earthquake exposure, supplier concentration links to VS-02.3 W558)

Network Strategy design resilience: backup DC sourcing (W4124), supplier diversification (links to VS-02.3 W763), multi-port inbound (W4125), buffer/pre-positioning (links to VS-02.3 W1432/W1492), and BCP alignment (VS-26)
Network Strategy stress-test the network (simulation W4143), incorporate risk-adjustment into design decisions, and report resilience to risk governance (VS-21.2/VS-26)

fields.Volume: Per major network change (DC add/close, lane re-design)

workflows.name: Network Design Business Case & Investment Planning

Automation Opportunity: - Business-case templates with industry benchmarks; sensitivity modeling
Controls: - CTL-638 (ensure controlled execution — Supply Chain Network Strategy, Modeling & Design (PA-136.1).)
- CTL-638: business case approved by Finance/Board; benefit reconciled post-implementation
Cross-references: - links to VS-40 (capex), VS-17.4 (finance), VS-133 W4065 (benefit), VS-112 (PMO), VS-134 (OCM)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Benefit-overstate risk**: Network savings overstated; mitigated by Finance sign-off and realization tracking
- **Execution-risk**: Good design, poor execution; mitigated by PMO/OCM integration
System Touchpoints: - Capex (VS-40); network model (W4122); benefit (VS-133 W4065); PMO (VS-112); governance (VS-36)

steps.activity: Network Strategy/Finance build the business case (capex, opex, working-capital, service, risk, sustainability), with TCO and benefit modeling, aligned to VS-133 W4065
Network Strategy/Finance model ROI/NPV/payback, test sensitivity, route via capex governance (VS-40) and Board approval (VS-36), and sequence with PMO (VS-112) and OCM (VS-134)
Network Strategy track realized benefit post-implementation (links to W4140), and feed lessons into future network design
